facts.fact: The ReCoDe local tax module is deployed after a census of taxable matter (TDRL and market and economic installations), with an electronic ticket coded for each taxpayer and a payment terminal (TPE) whose QR code feeds the town hall's server; in Bamako Commune VI in 2023 the census found 540 million FCFA, the estimate was set at 250 million, and 250 million FCFA was collected with the TPE and ReCoDe follow-up (Pro-ARIDES note, July 2024).

The data of the 13 Pro-ARIDES communes using ReCoDe are centralised on the central server at the DGCT, although the interconnection between the DGCT servers and the Treasury's DNTCP was still delayed in July 2024.
In April 2023 ReCoDe existed on the local network of 10 of the 13 Pro-ARIDES communes and had been tested there (for the other three, no information), with the town hall server holding the tickets.
The note says ReCoDe was deployed in 680 communes for testing, 13 of them Pro-ARIDES partners; it gives no denominator and does not say how many use the local tax module.

After training in 27 Pro-ARIDES communes, only Kava showed willingness to carry the tax digitalisation through; the note recommends a pilot phase in two to four communes, and says Bamako Commune VI's 2017 experience was not renewed in 2018.

ReCoDe was chosen by the national local finance committee (CNFL) and rolled out by the DGCT and the Treasury (DNTCP); the interministerial order setting the electronic collection arrangements required by article 58 of decree 2019-0587 had not been adopted between 2019 and mid-2024.

ReCoDe deployment in the Pro-ARIDES communes was financed by ANICT, LuxDev and, for San, EDREAS and PADRE III, with GIZ among the supporting partners; Pro-ARIDES is funded by the Netherlands and Denmark.

In February 2024 the commune of Kava opened an Orange merchant account for paying taxes, which works timidly because of a 1 per cent withdrawal fee; it deliberated to census its taxable matter and recruited a data-entry agent. The note also reports collectors destroying payment terminals with some elected officials' complicity (undated).
